rules.sentence: **The trigger is named by itself, never by the tooltip.** The element needs its own accessible name — visible text or an `aria-label` — and the component throws a named error when it has none. An icon-only Button carries `aria-label`; the tooltip may repeat the words for sighted users.

**The tooltip is a description.** The popup is `role="tooltip"`, and while it is rendered the trigger's `aria-describedby` points at it — and only then: no dangling reference when it is closed, and any description the trigger already had is kept.

**Hover waits, focus does not.** On hover it opens after `--vela-delay-tooltip` (600ms), read from the stylesheet, so a pointer crossing a toolbar does not flash every label; on keyboard focus it opens at once.
**Escape dismisses it** without moving focus or closing anything else.

**Never on a disabled control.** A disabled button takes no focus and, in most browsers, no pointer events, so its tooltip is unreachable — and why a control is disabled belongs in adjacent text (`DESIGN.md`, *States*). If a design insists, wrap the control in a focusable `<span tabIndex={0}>` with its own name and put the tooltip on that, and say so in review.
**Supplementary only.** Touch users never see a tooltip (Base UI disables them on touch), so it never carries the only copy of anything.
**In forced colours it keeps an edge.** The fill is replaced by `Canvas`, so the popup takes a 1px `CanvasText` border.

**It grows from its trigger, by transform and opacity alone.** Opened by a resting pointer it scales from 0.96 to full size as it fades in, pivoting on Base UI's `--transform-origin` — the edge nearest the trigger.
**Closed and reopened mid-flight, it turns round.** A pointer that comes back while it is fading out brings the same tooltip back from where it is; it ends open and at rest.
**From the keyboard it does not animate.** Focus opens it, and Escape closes it, at once.
**Under reduced motion it is at its end state.** Open is full size and opaque; closed is gone.
